Welcome & Introduction On May 28, 2025, the South Mediterranean University (MedTech), in collaboration with BIM Africa, proudly hosted BIM Day Tunisia 2025—a high-level, multidisciplinary forum dedicated to accelerating the adoption of Building Information Modeling (BIM) in Tunisia and across the African continent. The event convened over 200 professionals, academics, public officials, and industry leaders, creating a dynamic platform for critical reflection, strategic dialogue, and collaborative engagement around the digital transformation of the construction and built environment sectors. Supported by Archetype Group and our Platinum Sponsor ST2I – Autodesk Gold Partner, the conference emphasized the transformative role of digital technologies in enhancing construction efficiency, sustainability, and governance. BIM Day Tunisia 2025 marked a significant milestone in national and regional efforts to advance a more structured and holistic approach to digital construction practices. The event’s partnership with BIM Africa, a leading continental network promoting BIM knowledge and capacity building, amplified the scope of the discussions, offering comparative insights from various African contexts and fostering regional cooperation. This collaboration reaffirmed Tunisia’s strategic commitment to align with broader African digitalization agendas and to contribute meaningfully to the collective advancement of BIM across the continent. Objectives of BIM Day Tunisia 2025 The primary objectives of BIM Day Tunisia 2025 were to: Raise national and regional awareness of BIM as a process-driven methodology that extends beyond software to include standards, workflows, policy frameworks, and organizational transformation. Showcase international and African best practices, providing actionable insights that can inform the development of a national BIM strategy tailored to Tunisia’s socio-economic and institutional context. Identify structural and operational challenges hindering BIM adoption in Tunisia, including gaps in regulation, skills development, inter-agency coordination, and access to digital infrastructure. Promote cross-sectoral collaboration by fostering dialogue between academia, public institutions, and private industry to ensure cohesive and coordinated BIM implementation. Support education and capacity building by advocating for the integration of BIM competencies in academic curricula and the development of certification programs for professionals and public-sector stakeholders. Strengthen regional cooperation by engaging with BIM Africa and other continental partners to harmonize digital construction standards and promote knowledge transfer across borders. He identified three essential drivers: • A strong mandate or champion at leadership level • Initial budget allocation and ROI patience • A long-term strategic vision He reviewed global best practices: UK's Level 2 mandate, Singapore’s incentives, and Nordic open standards. Tunisia must tailor a national roadmap by integrating these lessons with local context. Anis Mahmoud – National Digitalization Report Anis Mahmoud presented insights from the Arab Institute of Business Leaders report, showing only 3% BIM penetration in Tunisia's construc- tion sector despite high opportunity recognition. Key benefits included early clash detection, reduced rework, and faster permit approvals. He highlighted challenges in software affordability and proposed negotiations with vendors for site licenses and local value creation. III. The University The Mediterranean Institute of Technology (MedTech) is a private, independent institution of higher education founded in 2012. The university offers a variety of bachelor’s and master’s degree programs, with the common feature of having a scientific and experimental research focus. The language of instruction is English. 1. History The Mediterranean Institute of Technology (MedTech) is the first English-speaking engineering school in Tunisia adopting an American curriculum. It was founded in 2012 by Professor Mahmoud Triki, Founder and President of the Mediterranean School of Business (MSB). Professor Triki aspired to make the university a regional hub of excellence in education, innovation, and entrepreneurship by offering a global education to students of the region and the continent. In fact, President Triki expressed the mission of the university in these words: “The strategic location of Tunisia in the heart of the Mediterranean, combined with the diversity of its cultural heritage, constitutes major assets for the development of a regional hub of educational excellence. Class meeting times are typically scheduled Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. Make-up classes may be scheduled on Saturdays, with at least a week’s notice from the professor or the administration. Academic Year and Class Schedules The academic year at MedTech consists of two terms: Fall (from September to December) and Spring (from January to May), and an optional summer term (from end May to end June). Each term stretches over 15 weeks (about 3 and a half months) except the summer session which stretches over four weeks only. Class meeting times are typically scheduled Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. Make-up classes may be scheduled on Saturdays, with at least a week’s notice from the professor or the administration.
